S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days after learning of it; incidents involving death, serious injury, or an active risk to the public must be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days after learning of it; incidents involving death, serious injury, or an active risk to the public must be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination. Reports shall include known unit/model identifiers, circumstances, and any corrective action; updates shall be provided as material facts become available.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model shall undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. Manufacturers shall provide complete per-model results, including protocol, sample size, and failure rate, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy or are considering buying that model; results may not be withheld from those customers as confidential. Exceeding 5% alone shall not automatically require withdrawal from the market; continued sale during remediation is subject to regulator-approved controls and timely retesting.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo sustained-heat testing at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative samples. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. Manufacturers shall provide complete per-model results, including protocol, sample size, and failure rate, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy or are considering buying that model; results may not be withheld from those customers as confidential. Manufacturers may publish results more broadly. A manufacturer whose model exceeds 5% shall notify the regulator within 30 days and submit a corrective-action and retesting plan. The regulator shall set a proportionate remediation timetable and may require interim risk controls based on the evidence. Exceeding 5% alone shall not automatically require withdrawal from the market; continued sale during remediation is subject to regulator-approved controls and timely retesting.

parameters.quote: All new home battery units placed on the market after adoption shall support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers shall equip previously installed units with this capability, or provide an equivalent regulator-approved emergency isolation measure, within 6 years after adoption.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: All new home battery units placed on the market after adoption shall support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers shall equip previously installed units with this capability, or provide an equivalent regulator-approved emergency isolation measure, within 6 years after adoption.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: All new home battery units placed on the market after adoption shall support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers shall equip previously installed units with this capability, or provide an equivalent regulator-approved emergency isolation measure, within 6 years after adoption. Manufacturers shall inform owners how shut-off works and how to request emergency activation. Shut-off systems shall be designed to remain secure against unauthorized access and shall not prevent safe local isolation.

parameters.quote: New home battery units placed on the market shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New home battery units placed on the market shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units placed on the market shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers shall provide installation and maintenance instructions and disclose any limitations of the suppression system to customers.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall provide customers clear safety notices about material risks, relevant incidents, and protective actions promptly, and no later than 5 business days after determining a material safety risk. A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; manufacturers shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate the recall, including instructions for safe shutdown, repair, replacement, or refund.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall provide customers clear safety notices about material risks, relevant incidents, and protective actions promptly, and no later than 5 business days after determining a material safety risk. A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; manufacturers shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate the recall, including instructions for safe shutdown, repair, replacement, or refund.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall provide customers clear safety notices about material risks, relevant incidents, and protective actions promptly, and no later than 5 business days after determining a material safety risk. Notices shall identify affected models and explain how customers can obtain applicable per-model thermal test results. A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; manufacturers shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and initiate the recall, including instructions for safe shutdown, repair, replacement, or refund. Regulators may require a recall or other protective action sooner where the evidence indicates an imminent or serious risk.

judge_section_notes: The final rules are mostly strict on reporting, testing, and recall triggers: all incidents reportable, 55°C/5% testing, mandatory recall at 8/100k. However, S2 allows continued sale during a regulator-set remediation timetable without a fixed end or interim cap, and S3 gives a long 6-year retrofit deadline. S4 and S5 include Halcyon's 36-month suppression phase-in and 5-business-day customer notices, but S5 lacks a mandatory serious-injury recall clause.
